newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end at new high on bullish sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end at new high on bullish sentiment.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished at another six-year high on Tuesday amid bullish sentiment, but brokers warned the risk of a correction increased as the index approached the 8,400-point resistance level.
Following an 8.26 point drop Monday, the benchmark stock index ended 72.46 points or 0.89 percent higher at 8,246.64.
Tuesday's close surpassed the 8,182.44 finish on March 8 and marked the index's highest level since it reached 8,569.55 on May 15, 1990.
Turnover was a hectic T$160.421 billion to the surprise of a number of brokers who had expected relatively smaller volume.
Most sectors saw gains -- with paper, steel and construction rising a respective 3.19 percent, 2.78 percent and 2.39 percent.
Taiwan Pulp and Paper gained T$2.10 to T$33.50, while China Steel advanced T$0.80 to T$27.30.
Yuh Chen Construction rose T$5.00 to T$77.50, and Da Cin Construction added T$3.00 to T$46.50.
"Strong market sentiment pushed the index to another new high," said Wang Tung-liang, executive vice-president of Jih Sun Securities.
He said the market was also buoyed by recent newspaper reports that the government planned to invest T$62 billion from the state labour insurance fund in stocks.
Brokers had predicted further consolidation for the index following its fall on Monday.
Lin Long-hsien, assistant manager of United Securities, said there was "behind-the-scenes support by major players".
But despite Tuesday's rise, analysts still saw profit-taking pressure emerging as the index, which has gained more than 1,200 points this year, approached a 8,400 resistance level.
A range of 8,200-8,300 was seen for Wednesday.
